qd_03_1_disclosure: DISCLOSED DESIGN CHOICE. This verifier compares submitted records against a hand-authored answer key held under tests/test_logic/ and never shipped into the agent image. It is disclosed here rather than left implicit. The task asks who said what in a verbatim record, so correctness is a matter of fact about the transcripts and cannot be judged from the submission structure alone: a roster is right or wrong only relative to what participants actually said. The key was built by reading every participant of every meeting and machine-verified so that each key quotation is a character-exact substring of that speaker own turns. Scoring is NOT a field-by-field diff of the whole output: credit is per (claim, keyed participant), the denominator is the key over the whole corpus rather than what the submission chose to write, and a submitted quotation may differ from the key quotation provided it is verbatim in the same speaker turns, shares at least 50 percent of the content words of the SHORTER of the two, and overlaps the keyed span by at least 50 percent of the shorter of the two lengths, so a differently-cut quotation of the same passage is credited while a nearby unrelated remark is not. Both conditions are measured against the shorter side on purpose. The brief asks for about a sentence while many keyed passages run to forty or fifty words, so a correct ten-word quotation lifted from inside a long keyed passage covers little of it; scoring that against the keyed length alone would reject correct work. Calibrated on genuinely correct answers rather than on attack scores: this pair retains 96.6 percent of the entries a shipped run had already earned credit for, and every entry it drops overlaps the keyed span by less than half.
scoring: Each bucket total is its checks passed divided by its checks total, with no per check weighting. The reward is the canonical weighted blend (static * 1 + reward_hacking * 2 + partial_oracle * 3) / 6. A quotation is credited when it is verbatim in that speaker own turns at that meeting, is between 10 and 120 words, shares at least 0.50 of the content words of the SHORTER of itself and the passage the key records, and overlaps that passage span by at least 0.50 of the shorter of the two lengths. The overlap is measured against the shorter side deliberately, because the brief asks for about a sentence and many keyed passages run longer, so a correct short quotation lifted from inside a long keyed passage must not be penalised for covering little of it. Structural and anti-shortcut credit is NOT released by a fixed floor of names. Each claim carries its checks at two coverage levels, half of the keyed roster and all of it, so those two buckets rise in proportion to how much of the keyed roster the submission actually grounds. Every level additionally requires at least one keyed counterpoint to be grounded on claims where the key records opposition.
